name: The rest of the Miami escort, at its camp (names not recorded)
head: miami_escort_1812_09
review_note: review_required: a Miami man of the escort William Wells brought from Fort Wayne, whom no source names. The owner asked (2026-11-08) that each be given a researched, respectful name and a history, both marked reconstructed (liberty L-1812-native-cards-3507). Nothing of the fighting is staged in the scene.

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: The escort's camp ground south-west of the fort (T-3499); where they camped is not recorded.

not_in_this_household.note: The people already carded at this ground have their own cards; everyone dealt here by docs/RESEARCH/gathering-people-1812-3500/build.py is on this one (liberty L-1812-gathering-people-3500).

card_facts.label: On 15 August
card_facts.value: Rode out with the column; did not fight

history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: He came from the Miami towns about Fort Wayne on the upper Wabash and the Maumee, by Fort Wayne, and rode to Chicago with William Wells's escort, which reached the fort on the 13th.
He is of the Raccoon gens (Ah-se-pon′-nä), and his children are of it after him.
The winter before, he hunted with his family on the Kankakee and traded the skins at Kinzie's for powder, cloth and kettles.
At Chicago he camps with the escort south-west of the fort, with his pony.

paragraphs: He came from the Miami towns about Fort Wayne on the upper Wabash and the Maumee, by Fort Wayne, and rode to Chicago with William Wells's escort, which reached the fort on the 13th.
He is of the Sun gens (Kul-swä′), and his children are of it after him.
In the spring he helped at the sugar camp, and in summer fished the river and the lake while the corn grew at the village.
At Chicago he camps with the escort south-west of the fort, with his pony.
